## Niche-specific ideas (26)

- **[Hyper-local conditional hook](../topics/hooks.md#hook-hyper-local-conditional)** (script): Call out a specific place and moment: "If you're going to Nehru Place or Lamington Road this weekend to build a PC, listen before you enter the shop…", with real market names as road-sign graphics.
- **[Intro = time, place, what's happening](../topics/story.md#story-time-place-intro)** (script): Open with the time, the place and what is going on in your life right now (the "3:47 a.m." intro); noticing what is in front of you is the material and should feel "warm to touch".
- **[Five yap frameworks; three carry 90%](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-takes-epiphanies-story)** (idea): Oren's five: strong take, strong take → education, small epiphany ("Do you notice how husbands always do this?"), humour (poke fun at something), story time. Takes, small epiphanies and story time are the foundation of ~90% of content.
- **[Even "here's three things" beats no frame](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-any-framework-beats-none)** (idea): Tristan: even a cringey "here's three things" does better than no framework; Briar lists "9 travel hacks" as a valid reach post while calling it "kind of cringe".
- **[Travel formats: vibe, dump, POV, "nobody tells you"](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-travel-formats)** (idea): Options: 10–12 s sunset vibe reel, camera-roll dump with text, "POV: your office trip actually turns out fun", "things nobody tells you about [place]" (saveable), scrapbook carousel with location labels, 30–45 s day-in-the-trip vlog.
- **[Office-trip content gets sent to colleagues](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-workplace-trip-shareable)** (idea): Workplace-trip content is highly shareable because people DM it to colleagues ("we need this trip"); the Khandala caption CTA asks to send it to the colleague who always says "next time".
- **[Name the exact spot everywhere](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-place-specific-seo)** (publish): Use the place plus the exact viewpoint in on-screen text, caption and location tag ("Khandala Lonavala" pairs well since people search both).
- **[End on a frame that loops](../topics/editing.md#edit-loop-to-frame-1)** (edit): Loopable edits win on watch time; the Khandala reel ends back on the sun and feet so it loops to frame 1.
- **[Cut on the beat or on motion](../topics/editing.md#edit-cut-on-beat-motion)** (edit): Our edit blueprint sets cut rules (on the beat or on motion) and travel uses a wide → close-up rhythm. Khandala cut every 1.5 s, which lands on 80 and 120 BPM beats (2 or 3 beats per shot), so music could be added later.
- **[Cull near-duplicates; keep the strongest](../topics/editing.md#edit-cull-near-duplicates)** (edit): Khandala: 43 raw files to 1 reel + 1 carousel; dropped near-duplicates, tilted horizons, soft digital zooms, litter in frame and harsh midday light that broke the sunset look.
- **[Trending audio only when it fits](../topics/sound.md#sound-trending-audio-fit)** (sound): Trending audio boosts discovery when it fits the format: energetic for gym transformations, nostalgic acoustic for travel recaps, spoken for skits; original voice-over builds connection.
- **[Export silent; pick a low-use track in-app](../topics/sound.md#sound-low-use-count-track)** (publish): Khandala was exported silent and the music chosen in Edits with the use count checked (under ~10K uses is ideal); a place-name song adds nostalgia. Our early edits went out silent this way (L02).
- **[Khandala pans and push-ins were linear](../topics/effects.md#fx-khandala-linear-moves)** (edit): Khandala animates its photos with slow pans and push-ins (sun to subject, cliff + cactus), but our ffmpeg build moved them at constant speed (linear), the opposite of L03's rule.
- **[Pan to reveal the subject](../topics/transitions.md#tr-pan-reveal)** (film): Khandala opens on a pan to the sun with feet coming into frame, then pans from sun to subject and reveals the peak.
- **[Serif italic emphasis + sans body](../topics/text.md#text-serif-italic-emphasis)** (graphics): Emphasis words in serif italic (*pro*, *honest*), body in clean sans, keyword highlights in yellow/orange. Our Khandala reel used Instrument Serif Italic.
- **[Hinglish voice and captions](../topics/text.md#text-hinglish-voice)** (script): Rahul speaks Hindi/Hinglish with English or Hinglish on-screen captions; our caption voice switches between English and Hinglish by theme (Khandala reel: Hinglish, chill).
- **[Golden-hour travel grade](../topics/colour.md#colour-golden-hour-grade)** (edit): Warm temperature, lifted shadows, highlights pulled to keep the sun's disc, richer oranges/yellows, sky blues nudged to teal, light grain; don't oversaturate greens.
- **[Khandala grade recipe in ffmpeg](../topics/colour.md#colour-khandala-ffmpeg-grade)** (edit): Gentle S-curve, warm mids/highlights (R +0.03), saturation 1.10, contrast 1.04, light vignette.
- **[Grade spec: exact sliders, presets per pillar](../topics/colour.md#colour-slider-spec-safe-bold)** (edit): Our grades list exact slider values with a reason each, a safe and a bold version, an orange-HSL skin check, and one reusable preset per pillar (gym = cool/contrasty, travel = warm/golden).
- **[iPhone 15: frame rates, modes, HDR](../topics/filming.md#film-iphone15-frame-rates)** (film): 4K 30 default; 4K 60 for reps you'll slow; 4K 24 for travel; 240 fps slo-mo for single moments; Action mode handheld; Cinematic mode for B-roll; HDR Video off for heavy grading (no Log/ProRes on the base 15).
- **[Lens choice: 1x low light, 0.5x daylight](../topics/filming.md#film-iphone15-lens-choice)** (film): The 1x 48 MP main lens is best in low light (gym, dusk); 0.5x ultra-wide only in good light; 2x for portraits and tighter muscle shots.
- **[Travel shots: silhouettes, backs, slow-mo](../topics/filming.md#film-travel-shots)** (film): Silhouettes against the sunset, group walking shots from behind, slow-motion hair/wind moments, wide → close-up rhythm.
- **[Ask before posting faces](../topics/filming.md#film-consent-faces)** (publish): Get a yes from everyone visible before posting or tagging; Khandala media stays outside the repo because colleagues appear in it.
- **[First 60 minutes after posting](../topics/growth.md#growth-first-60-minutes)** (publish): Share to Stories with a sticker/poll (Khandala: a "Guess the point?" poll), reply to every comment, DM it to a few friends who'd enjoy it.
- **[Moody grade: highlights down, blacks up](../topics/colour.md#l10-moody-grade-recipe)** (edit): His recommended look: curves pull the highlights down and lift the blacks, saturation down 15%, then a soft vignette. On-screen panel values: Highlights -35, Blacks +12, Saturation -15, Vignette -40. His own footage sits at mean luma ~25-28% with very low saturation and warm practical lamps.
- **[Before/after slider reveals the grade](../topics/effects.md#l10-grade-slider-reveal)** (edit): The source shows a warm look switched on, then a vertical slider wipes across to take it off: a before/after reveal. Chandler: FFmpeg makes the colour change, Remotion the slider.

## Memes (28)

- **Vine boom**: Realisation, shock, 'did he really just say that'. The universal punchline marker. Timing: Transient lands ON the reaction/punchline frame (frame 0 of the face or text). Freeze or hold 8-12 frames (0.27-0.4 s) at 30 fps, then cut. Never let it run under speech.
- **Sad violin / world's smallest violin**: Mock sympathy; first-world problem. Timing: Start on the 'sad' frame, duck everything else -12 dB, cut the violin hard at the next scene cut.
- **Record scratch + freeze ('Yep, that's me')**: Cold-open: start at the chaotic climax, then flash back. Timing: Scratch ends on the freeze frame; music must stop on the same frame. Hold freeze 45-60 frames for the VO line, then hard cut to 'earlier' card.
- **Anime 'wow' / 'sugoi'**: Exaggerated amazement at something mundane. Timing: Begin 2 frames before the reveal so the vowel peaks on the reveal frame.
- **Aura farming / aura points**: +1000 aura: calm flex, composure under pressure. '-500 aura' for a fail. Timing: Text '+1000 aura' pops on the downbeat (4-frame scale-in with overshoot); hold until next bar.
- **'Nah, I'd win' (Gojo, JJK)**: Confidence before facing something huge (a 3-plate deadlift, a boss, a 20-hour layover). Timing: Line ends 4-6 frames before the cut to the challenge; hold a stare 20 frames.
- **GTA 'Wasted'**: Total failure / comic death. Timing: Slow down to 30-40% speed over 6 frames on the fail, desaturate to grey over 15 frames, 'WASTED' text lands at frame ~20 with the sting; hold 45 frames.
- **Mario coin**: Small win, money saved, +1. Timing: On the frame the item/price/rep counter appears; stack on each item in a list (min 6 frames apart).
- **Secret discovered / item get**: Found something cool: a hidden cafe, a BIOS setting, a gym hack. Timing: Jingle's final note on the reveal frame; raise item over head (literally) for 30 frames.
- **Curb Your Enthusiasm outro ('Frolic')**: Awkward self-own ending; things went wrong in a comedic way. Timing: Freeze on the most awkward frame, music starts on that exact frame, 'Directed by Robert B. Weide' credit fades up ~1 s in; total 3-5 s.
- **SpongeBob time card ('A few moments later')**: Time skip (waiting for a flight, food, a render, a rest timer). Timing: Full-screen card 45-60 frames, hard cut in and out (no transition).
- **'Oh no, oh no, oh no no no no no'**: Disaster about to happen; anticipation of a fail. Timing: Start 1-1.5 s BEFORE the fail so the 'no no no' hits on it.
- **'To Be Continued' (Roundabout)**: Cliffhanger right before a disaster. Timing: Song intro starts ~2 s before the fail; freeze on the frame before impact; sepia + 'To Be Continued' arrow slides in from the left over 8 frames.
- **Wilhelm scream**: Cartoonish fall / someone 'dies' (wipeout). Timing: Starts on the frame the person loses balance.
- **Cartoon boing / slide whistle**: Silly bounce, sudden jump, things falling over. Timing: Boing on the bounce apex; slide whistle spans the fall (start on loss of balance, end on landing).
- **Law & Order 'dun-dun'**: Case closed / scene change with gravity. Timing: Over a black card with a location/time stamp; 2 hits 10 frames apart.
- **Jeopardy 'Think!' music / Kahoot lobby**: Waiting, thinking, loading. Timing: Under a time-lapse of waiting (render bar, queue, rest timer). Cut on any bar line.
- **Owen Wilson 'wow'**: Unimpressed/impressed sarcasm. Timing: On the reveal; hold 20 frames.
- **'Yippee!'**: Wholesome tiny win. Timing: On the success frame (bar locks out, package arrives, flight boards).
- **Dial-up modem**: Slow internet, old tech, 'loading...'. Timing: Over a frozen loading bar; cut at a screech peak.
- **Fake phone notification / message ping**: A text/DM arrives (from your gym bro, your mom, the airline). Timing: Notification banner slides down over 5 frames (ease-out) with the ding on its first frame.
- **Cha-ching cash register**: Money spent/saved, deal found, 'that's expensive'. Timing: On the price-tag reveal frame.
- **Heartbeat tension**: Nerves before a max attempt, landing approach, unboxing price. Timing: Beat interval shrinks toward the moment; silence on the moment itself (1 frame before the action), then hit.
- **Airplane cabin chime (seatbelt 'bing-bong')**: Departure/arrival, 'we are now landing', new chapter. Timing: On the cut to the window/wing shot; second tone on the title card.
- **'Where to next?' passport stamp / suitcase zip**: Trip announcement, next destination. Timing: Stamp thud on the frame the destination text slams in.
- **Camera shutter 'photo dump'**: Photo dump / still frame / 'snapshot'. Timing: Each still flashes white for 1 frame with the shutter on that frame; 6-10 frames per photo on the beat.
- **VHS rewind 'let's go back'**: Let's rewind to how this started / redo. Timing: Reverse the clip at 3-4x for 15-30 frames with the rewind sound; tape-stop on the last frame before a reset.
- **'Just a chill guy' lo-fi**: Unbothered calm while chaos happens. Timing: Bed at -22 dB under VO, text 'just a chill guy' as the hook in frame 0.
